Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 1975, after the draft finahzed by the Piezoelectric Devices Control and Selection Sectional Committee had been Electrotechnical Division Council. is to provide methods of measurement for over the frequency range up to 30 MHz.

0.2 The object of this standard piezoelectric vibrators operating

0.2.1 The transmission method described in this standard is suitable for frequencies up to 30 MHz for the commonly encountered ranges of the capacitance ratio r and the figure of merit M, provided that errors due to The equations presented in this instrumentation are taken into account. standard have been formulated to correct these errors. 0.3 In preparing this standard assistance has been derived from the IEC Pub 302-1969 `Standard definitions and methods of measurement for piezoelectric vibrators operating over the frequency range up to 30 MHz' issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960."

2. TERMINOLOGY describes the methods of measurement for piezoelectric over the frequency range up to 30 MHz.

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of terms given in IS : 1885 (Part V)-19657 and IS : 1885 (Part XXXIII)-19721 shall apply.

3.2 Equivalent Electric Circuit of a Piezoelectric Vibrator - The electrical behaviour of a lightly damped mechanical vibrating system which is excited piezoelectrically through electrodes forming a two-terminal network can be represented in the vicinity of any mechanical resonance by an equivalent electric circuit (see Fig. 1) which consists of a capacitance Cl, inductance L, and resistance R, in series, shunted by the parallel capacitance CO. The parameters are independent of frequency for isolated modes of motion. NOTE - Generally, the mode in question is sufficiently isolated from other modes to permit this assumption. When this is not true, the equations and measuring methods outlined herein do not apply.

4.2 Transmission

Measurement

Circuit

4.2.1 Figure 4 shows a schematic representation of the transmission The measuring circuit consists of a constant current source in the circuit. form of a variable frequency oscillator, the transmission network and a The piezoelectric vibrator is represented by its equivalent voltmeter. The network is symmetrical with respect to the input and electric circuit. output. The capacitances CT, which shunt the terminating resistances Rr, represent stray element which affect the accuracy of measurements as shown in Table 6. The oscillator shall have a high degree of purity of output waveform to an extent consistent with the requirements of the individual vibrator under test (see Note). NOTE- For most practical purposes, the following requirements are adequate: harmonics greater than 30 dB below the main signal, frequency stability better than 1 x 10-0 and amplitude change less than 10 percent during the measurement period. 10

OSCILL

ATOR

FIG. 4

SCHEMATIC DIAGRAM OF TRANSMISSION CIRCUIT METHOD

4.2.2 The inductance L,, connected across the vibrator, serves to resonate the shunt capacitance C, of the vibrator at fs. This added component improves the accuracy of measurement as explained in 4.3.1. 4.2.3 An important source of stray capacitance to ground that shall be considered occurs at the junction of the crystal unit and the capacitor Cr. (Fig. 4). This stray capacitance is composed of two parts: that associated with the crystal unit under test and that associated with CL. When the magnitude of these stray reactances is large compared with the magnitude of the termination impedance, the distributed capacitance to ground of the crystal unit and the distributed capacitance to ground of CL at the junction may be treated in a first approximation as being in parallel with CL. While measuring the parameters of crystal units by other than the transmission method, consideration shall be given to the stray capacitance of each terThis is of course an important conminal of the crystal unit to ground. sideration in the use of crystal units in network and frequency control applications. 4.2.4 The voltmeter which is placed at the output, e2 as the frequency of the input is varied. measures the voltage

4.3.4.2 In the case of vibrators with low figure of merit M, it is advisable to use a shunting coil Lo connected in parallel with the vibrator. 4.3.5.1 The shunt capacitance C, of the equivalent electric circuit of a vibrator is slightly smaller than the measured value for a free piezoelectric element and slightly greater than the measured value for a piezoelectric element in clamped condition. The exact value of the dielectric permittivity depends upon the mode of vibration. This has to be considered when greater accuracy is required.

IS : 7962 - 1975 4.3.5.2 There is no direct method for measuring CO precisely. However, in nearly all practical cases it is adequate to regard as CO the mean value of the shunt capacitances C,,, and C,,, of the resonator obtained at two frequencies, equidistant above and below the resonance frequency and sufficiently removed from the latter for the impedance to be independent of any response. C,,, and CO, can be measured by means of an impedance bridge or a Q-meter. 4.3.5.3 It should be noted that C,, is the shunt capacitance between the two electrodes of the resonator. As pointed out in 4.2, the capacitances of both of the electrodes to ground are important elements in many network and frequency control applications. Proper use of the transmission circuit method for the measurement of C, requires knowledge of at least the capacitance to ground of that electrode of the resonator which is connected to CL (see Fig. 4). 4.3.5.4 crystal unit capacitances measurements dealing with Therefore, in the general case, it is necessary to consider the as a three-terminal network and to evaluate C,, and the stray of the two electrodes to ground from open- and short-circuit according to the techniques customarily employed when two-port devices.

4.3.5.5 The crystal enclosure remains at ground potential during the entire series of measurements required for evaluation of the resonator parameters. For this purpose, it may be found desirable to provide glassenclosed crystal units with metal shells. 4.4 Numerical Examples deviation offs is given by: from its true values, due to detector
